Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

Source: Steps 6–9 of the parent proof = the printed displays (1)–(6) of the "Proof of 8.2" (pp. 176–178) with footnote 5 and the documented errata: "??(2) of Ch. 1" is the covering property 3.11(3) of Ch. 1 (every Radon measure on ℝ^P has the Symmetric Vitali Property; Besicovitch); in the justification of (3) the printed bound δ⁻¹f^{1/n}(δ) ≤ ω_n^{1/n}ε is corrected to δ⁻¹f^{1/n}(δ) ≤ (ω_nε)^{1/n}, so (3) reads (d/dr)f^{1/n}(r) ≤ 2(ω_nε)^{1/n} and (4) becomes M(S_r) ≤ c_2 ε^{1/(n−1)} M(T⌞B_r(ξ)) (n ≥ 2), with ε_0 chosen so that c_2ε_0^{1/(n−1)} ≤ ½; "σ, ρ" in footnote 5 mean ε. Filled in: (2) is derived from the integrated slicing inequality (4.10) of SlicingTheorem; the comparison currents from 6.1 are composed with a smooth radial compression so that their supports lie in B̄_{3r}(ξ) (needed for the printed cone estimate "by 2.27, 2.30"). Book n = m + 1 ≥ 1, P ≥ n + 1.

Hypotheses: m + 2 ≤ P; SlicingTheorem; IsoperimetricTheorem; LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity; (BLI) for Y_j, Y ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P): if every ∂Y_j is i.m., sup_j M(∂Y_j) < ∞ and ∂Y_j ⇀ ∂Y, then ∂Y is i.m.; T_j, T ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) with T_j i.m., ∂T_j = 0, Λ := sup_j M(T_j) < ∞, T_j ⇀ T. Goal: there is μ with IsMassMeasure T μ and Θ*ⁿ(μ,x) := dimensionalUpperDensity μ n ℝ^P x = limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) > 0 for μ-a.e. x.

Facts used. (F1) |Z(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖M_W(Z) if tsupport ω ⊆ W. (F2) If η, η′ agree on an open set containing spt Z then Z(η) = Z(η′). (F3) Lower semicontinuity of M_W under weak convergence (`WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf`). (F4) `iwl_restriction_theory`: (R1) uniqueness of restrictions; (R2) for currents of locally finite mass: mass measure, restrictions to all Borel sets, and M_W(Y⌞A) = μ_Y(W ∩ A) for open W. Through one fixed representation (μ_Y, v_Y) as in (R2), restrictions are countably additive in A and Y⌞ℝ^P = Y. (F5) The zero current has the representation (0, 0), so by (R1) every restriction of 0 is 0. (F6) (Radial homotopy operator.) For ξ ∈ ℝ^P and a j-form ω (j ≥ 1) put (H_ξω)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^{j−1}((x − ξ)⌟ω(ξ + t(x − ξ))) dt; then ω = d(H_ξω) + H_ξ(dω) (Cartan's homotopy formula for the homotopy from the constant map ξ to the identity; no constant-map term in degree j ≥ 1), and |H_ξω(x)| ≤ |x − ξ| ‖ω‖ (using |v⌟α| ≤ |v||α|).

1. (Preliminaries on T.) ∂T = 0: ∂T(ω) = lim ∂T_j(ω) = 0 (`WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary`). M(T) ≤ liminf M(T_j) ≤ Λ (F3), so T has locally finite mass; let μ := μ_T be its mass measure from (R2): IsMassMeasure T μ, μ(ℝ^P) = M(T) ≤ Λ, restrictions T⌞A exist for all Borel A, and M_W(T⌞A) = μ(W ∩ A). Write n := m + 1.
2. (Step 6 = printed (1): ∂(T⌞B_r(ξ)) is i.m. for a.e. r.) Fix ξ ∈ ℝ^P and d_ξ(x) := |x − ξ| (1-Lipschitz). For each j apply SlicingTheorem to T_j (U = ℝ^P; masses finite, ∂T_j = 0) with f := d_ξ, L := 1: slices S^j(t) with S^j(t) = ∂A^j_t − B^j_t, A^j_t a restriction of T_j and B^j_t a restriction of ∂T_j = 0 to {d_ξ < t}; by (F5) B^j_t = 0, so S^j(t) = ∂A^j_t; S^j(t) is i.m. for a.e. t; and for each N ∈ ℕ, with W := ℝ^P, L_W := 1, (a,b) := (0,N) and the restriction of T_j to {0 < d_ξ < N} (exists by (R2); its mass is ≤ M(T_j) ≤ Λ), there is a measurable g^N_j ≥ M(S^j(·)) on (0,N) with ∫⁻_{(0,N)} g^N_j ≤ Λ.
   Fix N. Apply `iwl_restriction_weak_limit` to X_j := T_j, X := T, W := B_{N+1}(ξ) (sup_j M_W(T_j) ≤ Λ), φ := d_ξ: a strictly increasing ψ and a countable E. By Fatou, h(t) := liminf_j g^N_{ψ(j)}(t) satisfies ∫⁻_{(0,N)} h ≤ Λ, so h < ∞ a.e. on (0,N). Let r ∈ (0,N) ∖ E with h(r) < ∞ and S^{ψ(j)}(r) i.m. for all j (a.e. r). Choose σ strictly increasing with sup_j M(S^{ψσ(j)}(r)) ≤ h(r) + 1. Let Y_j := A^{ψσ(j)}_r and Y := T⌞B_r(ξ) (a restriction of T to {d_ξ < r}). Since {d_ξ ≤ r} = B̄_r(ξ) is compact and contained in W, part (B) of `iwl_restriction_weak_limit` and (R1) give Y_j ⇀ Y (the restrictions of T_{ψ(j)} to {d_ξ < r} converge, and Y_j is the σ(j)-th of them), hence ∂Y_j ⇀ ∂Y. As ∂Y_j = S^{ψσ(j)}(r) is i.m. with sup_j M(∂Y_j) < ∞, (BLI) gives: ∂(T⌞B_r(ξ)) is i.m. Letting N run through ℕ: (1) ∂(T⌞B_r(ξ)) is i.m. for L¹-a.e. r > 0.
   Moreover, applying SlicingTheorem to T itself (∂T = 0, (F5), (R1)), its slice at r is ∂(T⌞B_r(ξ)), so spt ∂(T⌞B_r(ξ)) ⊆ spt T ∩ ∂B_r(ξ), a compact set; and ∂∂(T⌞B_r(ξ)) = 0.
3. (Step 7 = printed (2): M(∂(T⌞B_r(ξ))) ≤ f′(r) for a.e. r.) Let f(r) := μ(B_r(ξ)) (r > 0): nondecreasing and bounded by Λ, hence differentiable at a.e. r. By SlicingTheorem for T (f := d_ξ, W := ℝ^P, L_W := 1), for all rationals 0 ≤ a < b there is a measurable g_{a,b} with M(∂(T⌞B_t(ξ))) ≤ g_{a,b}(t) for t ∈ (a,b) and ∫_a^b g_{a,b} ≤ M(T⌞{a < d_ξ < b}) = μ({a < d_ξ < b}) ≤ f(b) − f(a) (mass identity, W = ℝ^P). Suppose, for some rational q > 0, the set E_q := {r : f′(r) exists and M(∂(T⌞B_r(ξ))) > f′(r) + q} had positive outer measure. Then so would E_{q,k} := {r ∈ E_q : kq/4 ≤ f′(r) < (k+1)q/4} for some k ∈ ℕ. Let H be a measurable hull of E_{q,k} and r* ∈ E_{q,k} a density point of H (a.e. point of H is one, and E_{q,k} has positive outer measure, so such r* exists). Let δ ∈ (0,1). For rationals a < r* < b close enough to r*: L¹(H ∩ (a,b)) ≥ (1 − δ)(b − a) and f(b) − f(a) ≤ (f′(r*) + q/8)(b − a). On E_{q,k} ∩ (a,b): g_{a,b}(r) ≥ M(∂(T⌞B_r(ξ))) > f′(r) + q ≥ f′(r*) + 3q/4 (as f′(r) ≥ kq/4 > f′(r*) − q/4). So the measurable set {r ∈ (a,b) : g_{a,b}(r) > f′(r*) + 3q/4} contains E_{q,k} ∩ (a,b) and therefore has measure ≥ L¹(H ∩ (a,b)) ≥ (1 − δ)(b − a). Hence (f′(r*) + q/8)(b − a) ≥ ∫_a^b g_{a,b} ≥ (f′(r*) + 3q/4)(1 − δ)(b − a), which is false once δ is small (f′(r*) < (k+1)q/4). So every E_q is null, i.e. (2) holds for a.e. r > 0.
4. (Step 8 = printed (3), (4), footnote 5: comparison surfaces.) Let ε ∈ (0, 1/8] and suppose Θ*ⁿ(μ,ξ) < ε. Then μ(B_σ(ξ)) ≤ μ(B̄_σ(ξ)) < εω_nσⁿ for all small σ > 0, so for all small δ > 0, since f^{1/n} is nondecreasing (the integral of the a.e. derivative of a monotone function is at most its increment; Mathlib `MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc`):
   δ⁻¹∫_0^δ (f^{1/n})′(r) dr ≤ δ⁻¹ f^{1/n}(δ) ≤ (ω_nε)^{1/n}   (corrected bound),
   and by Chebyshev's inequality the set G_δ := {r ∈ (0,δ) : (f^{1/n})′(r) exists and ≤ 2(ω_nε)^{1/n}} has measure ≥ δ/2 (3). The following conditions hold for a.e. r: (1), (2), f′(r) exists, (f^{1/n})′(r) exists, μ(∂B_r(ξ)) = 0 (fails only for countably many r, μ being finite). Choose r ∈ G_δ satisfying all of them, and let Z := ∂(T⌞B_r(ξ)) ∈ D_m(ℝ^P): i.m., compact support in ∂B_r(ξ), ∂Z = 0, M(Z) ≤ f′(r). We construct an i.m. S_r ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) with
   (4) spt S_r ⊆ B̄_{3r}(ξ), ∂S_r = Z, M(S_r) ≤ c_2 ε^{1/(n−1)} f(r) if n ≥ 2, M(S_r) = 0 if n = 1,
   where c_2 = c_2(n,P) is given below; note f(r) = μ(B_r(ξ)) = M(T⌞B_r(ξ)).
   (a) If f(r) = 0: then M(T⌞B_r(ξ)) = 0, so T⌞B_r(ξ) = 0 (F1) and Z = 0; put S_r := 0.
   (b) n = 1 (m = 0), f(r) > 0 (footnote 5): M(Z) ≤ f′(r) = (f^{1/1})′(r) ≤ 2ω_1ε = 4ε ≤ ½ < 1. A nonzero i.m. 0-current Z = Σ_{x∈M_Z} c(x)δ_x (c(x) ∈ ℤ∖{0}) has mass ≥ 1 (test with a bump function equal to sign c(x) near one point x ∈ M_Z, of sup norm 1, supported in a small ball around x avoiding the other points of the locally finite set M_Z: the value is |c(x)| ≥ 1). Hence Z = 0; put S_r := 0.
   (c) n ≥ 2 (m ≥ 1), f(r) > 0: write m′ := m − 1 and ℓ := P − n ≥ 1, so that P = m′ + 2 + ℓ and Z has degree m′ + 1. By IsoperimetricTheorem (for m′, ℓ, after rewriting the ambient dimension P = m′ + 2 + ℓ) there are c_1 = c_1(n,P) ≥ 0 and an i.m. S′ ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) with compact support, ∂S′ = Z and M(S′)^{(n−1)/n} ≤ c_1 M(Z). Since f = (f^{1/n})ⁿ, f′(r) = n f(r)^{(n−1)/n} (f^{1/n})′(r) ≤ 2n(ω_nε)^{1/n} f(r)^{(n−1)/n}, so M(S′)^{(n−1)/n} ≤ 2c_1 n (ω_nε)^{1/n} f(r)^{(n−1)/n}, i.e.
   M(S′) ≤ (2c_1 n)^{n/(n−1)} (ω_nε)^{1/(n−1)} f(r) =: c_2 ε^{1/(n−1)} f(r), c_2 := (2c_1n)^{n/(n−1)} ω_n^{1/(n−1)}.
   (Support control.) Let h ∈ C^∞(ℝ), 0 ≤ h ≤ 1, h = 1 on (−∞, 2r], h = 0 on [5r/2, ∞); κ(s) := ∫_0^s h; Φ(x) := ξ + κ(|x − ξ|)(x − ξ)/|x − ξ| (Φ(ξ) := ξ). Φ = id on B_{2r}(ξ), so Φ is C^∞ on ℝ^P; |Φ(x) − ξ| ≤ ∫_0^∞ h ≤ 5r/2; and ‖DΦ(x)‖ ≤ 1, since for x ≠ ξ, with u := (x − ξ)/|x − ξ| and s := |x − ξ|, DΦ(x) = κ′(s) u⊗u + (κ(s)/s)(I − u⊗u) has eigenvalues h(s) ∈ [0,1] and κ(s)/s ∈ [0,1]. Apply `iwl_smooth_pushforward` to X := S′ (i.m., degree n = k + 1 with k = m), f := Φ, U = V = ℝ^P (spt S′ compact, so properness holds): an i.m. S_r ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) with S_r(ω) = S′(η) and ∂S_r(ω′) = ∂S′(η′) = Z(η′) whenever η, η′ agree with Φ^#ω, Φ^#ω′ near spt S′, and M(S_r) ≤ M(S′) (c = 1). Then: ∂S_r = Z, because Φ^#ω′ = ω′ on B_{2r}(ξ) (Φ = id there) and spt Z ⊆ ∂B_r(ξ) ∩ spt S′, so η′ = ω′ near spt Z and Z(η′) = Z(ω′) (F2); spt S_r ⊆ B̄_{5r/2}(ξ) ⊆ B̄_{3r}(ξ), because if tsupport ω ∩ B̄_{5r/2}(ξ) = ∅ then Φ^#ω = 0 (Φ maps into B̄_{5r/2}(ξ)), so S_r(ω) = S′(0) = 0; and M(S_r) ≤ c_2 ε^{1/(n−1)} f(r).
   Since δ was arbitrary, for every ξ with Θ*ⁿ(μ,ξ) < ε there are arbitrarily small radii r with (4) and μ(∂B_r(ξ)) = 0.
5. (Step 9 = printed (5), (6): covering.) Fix ε := ε_0 := min{1/8, (2c_2)^{−(n−1)}} if n ≥ 2 (ε_0 := 1/8 if n = 1; if c_2 = 0 take ε_0 := 1/8), so that M(S_r) ≤ ½ f(r) in (4). Let C be a compact subset of A_0 := {x : Θ*ⁿ(μ,x) < ε_0} and δ_0 > δ > 0; put C_s := {x : dist(x,C) < s}. The closed balls B̄_r(ξ) with ξ ∈ C, r < δ, satisfying (4) and μ(∂B_r(ξ)) = 0 cover C finely, so by the Besicovitch covering theorem for the finite Radon measure μ on ℝ^P (Simon Ch. 1, 3.11(3) and 3.10; Mathlib `Besicovitch.exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae`) there is a countable pairwise disjoint subfamily B_i := B̄_{r_i}(ξ_i) with μ(C ∖ ⋃_iB_i) = 0; also ⋃_iB_i ⊆ C_δ ⊆ C_{δ_0}. Let S_i := S_{r_i} (centred at ξ_i). Since μ(∂B_{r_i}(ξ_i)) = 0, T⌞B_i = T⌞B_{r_i}(ξ_i) (their difference is T⌞∂B_{r_i}(ξ_i), of mass μ(∂B_{r_i}(ξ_i)) = 0).
   (a) Z_i := S_i − T⌞B_i satisfies ∂Z_i = 0, spt Z_i ⊆ B̄_{3r_i}(ξ_i), M(Z_i) ≤ M(S_i) + μ(B_i) ≤ (3/2)μ(B_i).
   (b) (Cone estimate, printed "by 2.27, 2.30".) For ω ∈ D^n(ℝ^P): |Z_i(ω)| ≤ 3r_i M(Z_i)‖dω‖. Indeed, take ζ ∈ C_c^∞(B_{3r_i+τ}(ξ_i)), 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 near B̄_{3r_i}(ξ_i) (τ > 0). By (F2) and (F6) (degree n ≥ 1, centre ξ_i): Z_i(ω) = Z_i(ζω) = Z_i(ζ d(H_{ξ_i}ω)) + Z_i(ζ H_{ξ_i}(dω)); the first term equals Z_i(d(ζH_{ξ_i}ω)) − Z_i(dζ ∧ H_{ξ_i}ω) = ∂Z_i(ζH_{ξ_i}ω) − 0 = 0; the second is bounded by ‖ζH_{ξ_i}(dω)‖M(Z_i) ≤ (3r_i + τ)‖dω‖M(Z_i) (F1, F6). Let τ ↓ 0.
   (c) Σ_iμ(B_i) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) ≤ Λ, so Σ_i M(Z_i) ≤ (3/2)Λ and X_δ(ω) := T(ω) + Σ_i Z_i(ω) converges absolutely; X_δ is linear and sequentially continuous (|Σ_iZ_i(ω)| ≤ (3/2)Λ‖ω‖), so X_δ ∈ D_n(ℝ^P), and by (b), |X_δ(ω) − T(ω)| ≤ Σ_i 3r_iM(Z_i)‖dω‖ ≤ (9/2)δΛ‖dω‖. Hence (6) X_δ ⇀ T as δ ↓ 0 (along any sequence δ_l ↓ 0).
   (d) By countable additivity of restrictions (one representation of T), T = T⌞(ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_iB_i) + Σ_i T⌞B_i, so X_δ = T⌞(ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_iB_i) + Σ_i S_i. For the open set V := C_{δ_0} and δ < δ_0, using subadditivity of mass and the mass identity:
   M_V(X_δ) ≤ μ(V ∖ ⋃_iB_i) + Σ_i M(S_i) ≤ μ(V ∖ C) + ½Σ_iμ(B_i) ≤ μ(V ∖ C) + ½μ(V),
   because μ(C ∖ ⋃_iB_i) = 0 and ⋃_iB_i ⊆ V (disjoint).
   (e) By (F3) and the mass identity, μ(V) = M_V(T) ≤ liminf_{l} M_V(X_{δ_l}) ≤ μ(V ∖ C) + ½μ(V); as μ(V) ≤ Λ < ∞: μ(C_{δ_0}) ≤ 2μ(C_{δ_0} ∖ C). As δ_0 ↓ 0 the sets C_{δ_0} ∖ C decrease to ∅ (C is closed), so μ(C) ≤ μ(C_{δ_0}) ≤ 2μ(C_{δ_0} ∖ C) → 0: μ(C) = 0.
6. (Conclusion.) Θ*ⁿ(μ,·) is a Borel function (Simon Ch. 1, Remark 3.2), so A_0 is Borel; by inner regularity of the finite Borel measure μ on ℝ^P and step 5, μ(A_0) = sup{μ(C) : C ⊆ A_0 compact} = 0. Hence Θ*ⁿ(μ,x) ≥ ε_0 > 0 for μ-a.e. x, and μ satisfies IsMassMeasure T μ. This is the required conclusion (with μ.toOuterMeasure in dimensionalUpperDensity and the exponent (m+1 : ℕ) : ℝ). ∎
key_steps: μ := μ_T from iwl_restriction_theory; ∂T = 0 and M(T) ≤ Λ.
(1): for a.e. r, ∂(T⌞B_r(ξ)) is integer multiplicity (slicing, Fatou, iwl_restriction_weak_limit, (BLI)).
(2): M(∂(T⌞B_r(ξ))) ≤ f′(r) for a.e. r, f(r) = μ(B_r(ξ)), from the integrated slicing bound and density points.

(3)–(4) with corrected constant: where Θ*ⁿ(μ,ξ) < ε there are small r with (f^{1/n})′(r) ≤ 2(ω_nε)^{1/n}; footnote 5 for n = 1; isoperimetric theorem plus radial compression (iwl_smooth_pushforward) give S_r with ∂S_r = ∂(T⌞B_r), spt S_r ⊆ B̄_{3r}(ξ), M(S_r) ≤ c_2ε^{1/(n−1)}μ(B_r(ξ)).
Besicovitch covering, the cone estimate |Z_i(ω)| ≤ 3r_iM(Z_i)‖dω‖, X_δ ⇀ T and lower semicontinuity give μ(C) = 0 for every compact C ⊆ {Θ* < ε_0}.
Hence Θ*ⁿ(μ,x) ≥ ε_0 > 0 for μ-a.e. x.
